gen-gf-slackey-instrument-sans: Slackey stands tall and sturdy, its letters spaced out with room to spare and its crossbars a notch lighter than the uprights. And Instrument Sans follows in bent-wire curves that never change weight, with c endings pointing apart.
gen-gf-slackey-inter: Expressive and a little cheeky, Slackey gives its tall letters gentle thickening and thinning, while Inter underneath is a plain sans cut at one width. One performs, the other simply informs.
gen-gf-slackey-mulish: Mulish has a big x-height, short ascenders and no thick-and-thin variation at all. Make Slackey small and its sturdy, widely spaced letters lose their swagger, so it wants the larger size.
gen-gf-slackey-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab packs the middle of each line with dense, structured texture, and its a, c, e and s stay open. Slackey beside it is the livelier, more expressive half.
gen-gf-slackey-rubik: Slackey's tall, sturdy lowercase and long gaps between letters make it the showman of the pair, with Rubik beside it as a soft sans. Rubik's lowercase looks big next to its capitals and stays open and clear.
gen-gf-sn-pro-fs-literata: Literata brings a bookish serif voice, with thin lines slightly lighter than its thick ones and wide-mouthed curves. SN Pro opens its own curves like a rope's bight, so it feels modern against that.
gen-gf-snippet-fs-literata: Approachable Snippet bends its tube-like strokes without ever letting the curve tips touch, like neatly shaped pipe cleaner. Literata, a bookish serif with modest stress, gives it a more sophisticated partner.
gen-gf-sometype-mono-fs-bespoke-sans: Sometype Mono is fixed-width and code-like, with diagonals as heavy as its verticals. It earns its place in big, short lines, while Bespoke Sans stays sharp with generous gaps at its curve ends.
gen-gf-sour-gummy-fs-literata: Sour Gummy's a opens its lower bowl so it can breathe. Literata, a text serif with fuller stems and slimmer links, gives that a soft, bookish partner that feels sophisticated beside it.
gen-gf-special-gothic-fs-literata: Literata reads like a bookish serif, its sturdy thin lines just lighter than the thick ones and its curves wide open. Over long paragraphs it stays gentle, while Special Gothic keeps a modern edge.
